title: Split EnforcementRunner.kt under the 250-line cap
objective: Bring focus_owner/android/.../EnforcementRunner.kt (564 lines) under the repo-wide 250-line cap by extracting cohesive concerns into standalone files, without changing EnforcementRunner's public API or EnforcementRunnerBestTest.kt's direct call to EnforcementRunner.best(...).
acceptance_criteria: bash meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh --all no longer lists EnforcementRunner.kt.

EnforcementRunner still exposes decide(), apply(decision, bridge), setHomeToCurrentLocation(), hasHomeLocation(), acquireLocation(...), and the companion best(...) with identical signatures, since MainActivity.kt and EnforcementRunnerBestTest.kt call these directly.
gradlew compileDebugKotlin --rerun-tasks succeeds with no compile errors.
gradlew test --rerun-tasks succeeds with the same test count (40) and zero failures as before the split, with EnforcementRunnerBestTest's 6 tests specifically still passing unmodified.
No method body logic changed -- only extraction into new files plus delegate wiring.
out_of_scope: Adding new unit tests for EnforcementRunner's decide()/apply() (they depend on Android system services not unit-testable without instrumentation; no prior test existed for them and none is required for a pure extraction).
Touching MainActivity.kt or EnforcementService.kt, whose call sites were verified but not modified.
Further splitting the remaining focus_owner Kotlin/Dart files or any of the other 8 files still over the 250-line cap.
verifier: JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk ./gradlew compileDebugKotlin test --rerun-tasks (from focus_owner/android), plus bash meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh --all showing EnforcementRunner.kt no longer over cap.
